options.why: solved for $u=e^x$ as $3, 4$ but forgot to take natural logarithms to find $x$
used the linear and constant coefficients of the quadratic equation as arguments
used incorrect negative signs when solving $e^x = 3$ and $e^x = 4$
did not reject the extraneous root $u=-3$, which has no real logarithm
gave the quadratic root $u=7$ rather than solving $e^x = 7$
incorrectly replaced $\ln(-3)$ with $-\ln 3$ instead of rejecting the negative root

questions.solution_text:
Let $u=e^x$.
$u^2 - 4u - 21 = 0$
$(u-7)(u+3) = 0$
$u=7 \text{ or } u=-3$
Since $e^x > 0$ for all real $x$, $e^x = -3$ has no solution.
$e^x = 7 \implies x = \ln 7$

options.why: kept the invalid negative root $u=-3$ instead of discarding it
ignored signs and treated negative roots as positive arguments

questions.solution_text:
Let $u=e^x$.
$2u^2 + 5u - 3 = 0$
$(2u-1)(u+3) = 0$
$u = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{ or } u = -3$
Since $e^x > 0$, $u=-3$ is rejected.
$e^x = \dfrac{1}{2} \implies x = \ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = -\ln 2$

questions.solution_text:
Let $u=\ln x$.
$u^2 - 7u + 10 = 0$
$(u-2)(u-5) = 0$
$u=2 \text{ or } u=5$
$\ln x = 2 \implies x = e^2$
$\ln x = 5 \implies x = e^5$
$x = e^2, e^5$

incorrectly rejected the negative logarithm value $u=-2$, which is valid and gives $x=2^{-2}=\dfrac{1}{4}$
computed $2 \times 4 = 8$ instead of $2^4 = 16$
kept the negative root $u=-1$ after multiplying by $e^x$
stopped at the quadratic roots $u=6, -1$ without solving $e^x = u$
used the constant term $5$ from the original equation as a solution

questions.solution_text:
Multiply both sides by $e^x$:
$e^{2x} - 6 = 5e^x$
$e^{2x} - 5e^x - 6 = 0$
Let $u=e^x$:
$u^2 - 5u - 6 = 0$
$(u-6)(u+1) = 0$
$u=6 \text{ or } u=-1$
Since $e^x > 0$, $u=-1$ is rejected.
$e^x = 6 \implies x = \ln 6$
